chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about buying silver that contains mercury and lead with silver coins, while, when it is melted, it decreases by two or three dirhams out of every ten.
So he عليه السلام said: “It is not valid except with gold.”

key_terms.أُذِيبَتْ: was melted down for testing or refining
key_terms.الذَّهَبِ: gold, the permitted counter-value in this exchange
key_terms.الْفِضَّةِ: silver as a monetary metal or commodity
key_terms.الْوَرِقِ: silver coinage or coined silver used in exchange

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy impure or mixed silver with silver coins in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on exchanging silver that is mixed with other substances and loses weight when refined. It indicates that such silver should not be purchased with silver coins, but may be exchanged with gold, reflecting rules meant to avoid invalid or usurious exchange in monetary transactions.
